neighbours.label: the preposition that assigns an object a role: 'have a carpenter for a brother-in-law', 'adults as their primary partners', 'use X as the value for the seed'
fire: My neighbour is lucky enough to have a plumber for a father, so leaks never last.
The children used an old blanket as a roof for their fort.
The script takes the current date as the name of the backup folder.
We hired a retired teacher as our guide for the museum tour.
She chose a quote from her grandmother as the title of the book.
The startup picked a former banker for its first chief executive.
Set the user's id as the key for each row in the cache.
He grew up with three sisters for company on the farm.
quiet: My neighbour's father is a plumber, so leaks in our street never last long.
The children built a fort out of chairs and an old blanket.
The script names the backup folder automatically every night.
A retired teacher showed us around the museum on Sunday.
Her grandmother liked to quote poems at the dinner table.
The startup's first chief executive used to work at a bank.
Each row in the cache stores the user's id and their last login.
He grew up on a farm with three sisters and a dog.

notes: Card peaks: ' in' x6, ' as' x6, ' for' x5; the strongest are role-assigning ('a chippie for a brother-in-law', 'adults as their primary communicative partners', 'epoch as the value for the seed', 'non-string values for lookups').
